title: Indefinite Hiatus
dek: On the H3 show and the word they used
kicker: A Pamphlet on the Klein Separation
subject: The H3 podcast and the Klein separation
voice_note: Written in the voice of Ernest Hemingway (1899–1961), through the writer-hemingway skill. An emulation — the prose and judgments are not the historical Hemingway's own words. Facts are drawn from reporting of October 22–24, 2026: Hila Klein's post, Ethan Klein's public response, the H3 production crew's statement, and the show's hiatus. The affair is as reported and is not independently confirmed. The other person is not named.
body:
On the twenty-second of October the wife put it on Instagram.

* * *

She said that for six months she had been given reasons that were not true. She said it started, as she had been told, as only a kiss. Then it was called emotional cheating. Then he said there had been an affair, and that it had run for more than six months.

The other person was not named. Nobody here will name her.

* * *

The show had already stopped. It went on indefinite hiatus just before the post. It was called H3 and it had been on for years, and now it was off.

* * *

He said he was asking for his family's privacy. He said he was working with his wife to take his ownership out of the podcasts, and out of Teddy Fresh and Teddy Glow, and out of any venture where he would make money from it.

He did not say how long the paperwork would take. Paperwork is slow. It is the one thing in the story that nobody has to rush.

* * *

She said they had separated. She said the children were in it too. She did not say how many there were, and the reports did not either.

She said they were in survival now. That was her word.

* * *

The crew made a statement. They said they were disgusted by what he had done and by the hurt it had caused. They said they stood with her. They said they would not work with him again, and would not profit from him.

That was done in the open, with names on it. It was the only part of the business that had been done with the hands.

* * *

Nobody in it used the word glory. Nobody used honor.

They used privacy, and survival, and disgusted. Each of them picked the one word he had for the thing. None of the words was the thing.

* * *

Every day the show had been on, people had sat down in front of the microphones and talked. Now nobody sat down.

That was the change. Nothing else in it changed that day.

* * *

He had asked for privacy. It was the one thing he asked for that could be given.

The show did not come back. The marriage was not said to be coming back either.

* * *

In the statements the word was indefinite.

Nobody said when the show would start again. Nobody said when he would say anything else. He had said he would give up what he owned in it. He did not say what he would keep.

It was indefinite. Nobody had to say when.
